content.title: About
content.content: Cooked pumpkin is the mature fruit of the pumpkin plant (Cucurbita pepo) that has been peeled, seeded and boiled until tender. It has a mild sweet flavor, soft texture and bright orange color. Cooked pumpkin is commonly used in soups, purees, casseroles and desserts.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Pumpkin belongs to the Cucurbitaceae family and is a relative of cucumbers, zucchini and melons.
The orange hue comes from high levels of beta‑carotene, a provitamin A pigment.
Pumpkin was domesticated more than 7,000 years ago in Central America.
In the United States, baked pumpkin is a Thanksgiving staple, but boiled pumpkin is often used for creamy soups.
Pumpkin seeds, often removed before cooking, are rich in zinc and magnesium.

items.title: Rich in beta‑carotene
items.content: Beta‑carotene is converted to vitamin A in the body, supporting vision, immunity and skin health.

items.title: Low in calories
items.content: 100 g of cooked pumpkin provides about 20 kcal, making it an excellent choice for weight‑controlled diets.

items.title: Source of dietary fiber
items.content: Fiber aids digestion, promotes satiety and supports a healthy gut microbiome.

items.title: Contains potassium
items.content: Potassium helps regulate fluid balance and blood pressure.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: In addition to beta‑carotene, pumpkin provides vitamin C and other phytochemicals that protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: A small number of people may experience allergic reactions to pumpkin or its seeds.

items.title: Sugar content
items.content: Although low in calories, pumpkin contains natural sugars that should be considered by people with diabetes.

items.title: Food safety
items.content: If cooked at too low a temperature or stored for too long, bacterial growth can occur.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Cooked pumpkin can be served as a side dish, added to soups, purees, salads, porridges, or used in baking. It also works well as a base for creamy soups, sauces and baby foods.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store cooked pumpkin in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3–4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑size bags for up to 2 months. Discard if it develops an off‑smell or slimy texture.
